summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload with AWS credential access
details: The package's `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) is an obfuscated loader (`_0xNNNN` identifiers, opaque dispatcher objects) that downloads the Bun runtime from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases` into a temporary directory and uses that alternate runtime to execute the adjacent 727 KB `math_init.js` file. `math_init.js` is a Bun-compiled `// @bun @bun-cjs` blob consisting of a giant numeric constant array plus a `WV8StW` string-array shuffle routine — the standard obfuscated hidden-payload shape — and contains multiple `.aws` string occurrences and `child_process` references, consistent with reading the installer's AWS credential paths (`~/.aws/`) and shelling out. Executing the payload under Bun instead of Node means Node-based scanners and lifecycle-hook analyzers never observe what runs. A React PDF-editor library has no legitimate reason to fetch a second language runtime at install time and execute a heavily obfuscated 727 KB blob under it. The combination of alternate-runtime dropper + install-time trigger + obfuscation + installer AWS credential paths reachable from the payload matches an active credential-harvesting supply-chain attack.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
